doc.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Barred from the University of Detroit; riding in the trunk to Pepper's house
summary: Fuller was turned away at the Catholic U of D, had lessons downtown, and hid in a car trunk to visit Pepper Adams.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Let’s flip back to Detroit. You mentioned Joe Henderson. So, just talk about your time at Wayne State and what was going on during that period.
Well, I tried to get in where Fred was. Fred was over at U of D out on Myers in Detroit.

Fred Mergy, this guy that played like Rosolino or better. The were Catholic over there at the University of Detroit. They didn't have any black kids over there. They finally got one, and they made a basketball star one everybody was pressed to have a black athlete. I forget his name, but he married Yvonne.
Was he like seven feet tall?
Yeah, Yvonne. He married the same girl that was married to…
You're not talking about Spencer Haywood?
I think I am. Yeah, that was his name. Haywood, he was married to Yvonne first.
Yeah, but he came out early.

So, he was allowed to go over there but I got off the bus once and they told me, "Get on the bus and go back where you came from.” So, I had to take my lessons from Elmer James at the music hall in downtown Detroit. I wasn't allowed in one part of downtown Detroit. I wasn't allowed to go out there. In fact, when I went to Pepper Adams house, a couple times I had to go into the trunk of the car during the day. I couldn't be seen riding in town with him. When I went into the service my two best friends, one of them’s father’s name is Gerald Utz. Utz, his father owned the potato chip thing there. And we were boys when I got in the first lack position in the Army band, and the mixer. They would come home during the weekend, his brother—not his brother, his best friend was an Italian kid who introduced me to pepperoni. She was in the box of pepperoni sticks and I would get two or three of them and that turned me on. That would last me a month and then it was gone. Cannon would be eating all my food. “Are you going to eat this potatoes? Are you going to check them out?” He followed me on the line on my shift. But, Pepper, his mother was a teacher. He was very proper at the time. His first name was Park Adams. His best bud was not me, it was Elvin Jones.
